messages:
maria: Heads up — after the v7 tokenizer patch rolled ~2h ago we started seeing a p99 jump (~+300ms) and a 15% throughput drop on hosted clusters. Noticed it when running the standard perf smoke checks :eyes:
ken: confirmed. Kernel selector started preference-flipping on long sequences, picking a fallback_fp16 kernel instead of the optimized fused attention. Lots of small batches too.
zane: infra signal: host-14 and host-22 show elevated iowait and cpu steal around the same timestamps. Possible noisy-tenant affecting kernel perf.
maria: repro steps I used:
```
# synthetic test hitting the same model + seq-dist
python perf_runner.py --model rdm-v7 --seq-len 1024 --qps 50 --duration 300
```
results: p50 ~ stable, p95 +100ms, p99 +300ms
ken: dug into profiler on a hot pod, pasted top hotspots: 
```
Profiler snapshot 2026-03-18T08:15Z
- fused_attention_kernel_v2: 28%
- fallback_attention_fp16: 47% (higher latency per-call)
- kv_cache_lookup: 9%
- batch_merger: 6%
- cuda_memcpy: 4%
```
ken: the selector heuristics seem to flip when batcher sees many short prefixes then long continuation — the kernel cost model picks fallback_fp16 because it underestimates prefix overhead.
ash: @maria are you seeing kv cache hit rate change?
maria: yes — kv-hit dropped from 88% to 60% on affected pods. Eviction spikes aligned with tokenizer producing more subtokens per word (subtokenization shift).
dash: so tokenizer change increased avg token-per-word causing smaller batches and more unique prefixes => kvcache misses + less batching => kernel chooses the wrong path.
ash: can we correlate user seq-length distribution pre/post rollout?
ken: pulled seq-dist histograms: pre-rollout median tokens/request 48, post-rollout median 62, 95th moved from 220 -> 430. More long tails.
dmitri: I pushed a quick experiment: pin kernel selection to fused_attention_kernel_v2 on one canary host and re-ran the perf smoke. p99 reduced by ~180ms on that host.
maria: good quick proof.
zane: infra mitigations while we fix selector heuristics: 1) auto-route high-p99 traffic to Dedicated pool with pinned kernels, 2) throttle noisy tenant on host-14, 3) increase kvcache size on hot hosts temporarily.
deploy-bot: rollout v7-tokenizer -> canary host-7: SUCCESS at 2026-03-18T08:40Z
ash: plan: rollback tokenizer patch for hosted until we deploy selector fix OR deploy kernel selector patch that better weights prefix cost + kvcache miss penalty. Which is faster?
ken: selector tweak is low-risk — I can push a candidate that increases prefix penalty and biases toward fused kernel when kvcache hit < 70%. Needs a short canary (30m).
maria: agree. Also add short-term rate limit for the noisy tenant and increase cache capacity as @nz suggested.
dmitri: created issue INF-4312 with traces, profiler snapshots, and test artifacts. Assigning to @ken for selector patch and @zane for infra mitigations.
ash: @oncall please monitor p99 and kv-hit dashboards, set alert threshold to p99 > 250ms for this model.
ash: thanks everyone — let's try selector canary, if green we roll to prod and keep tokenizer change paused for hosted. :thumbsup:
